text: With George Willard beside him, Wing lost some of his timidity, and the shadowy self usually buried under his doubts came out to look at the world. <break time="0.8s" /> When he talked with the young reporter, his voice, which had been low and trembling, became loud and sharp, and his bent body straightened. <break time="0.8s" /> Then his slender, expressive fingers would begin to beat upon a table or the top board of a fence, and this seemed to make him more comfortable. <break time="0.8s" /> The story of Wing Biddlebaum is a story of hands, and their restless activity, like the beating wings of a caged bird, had given him his name. <break time="0.8s" /> Wing tried to keep his hands hidden, and he looked with wonder at the quiet hands of other men who worked beside him in the fields. <break time="0.8s" /> In Winesburg the hands had attracted attention merely because of their activity, and with them he had once picked as many as a hundred and forty quarts of strawberries in a day. <break time="0.8s" /> The town was proud of his hands in the same way that it was proud of Banker Whites new stone house and Wesley Moyers trotting stallion, Tony Tip. <break time="0.8s" /> Although George Willard had often felt a strong curiosity about the hands, only his growing respect for the old man had kept him from asking.
